        COMMENTS OF THE INDEPENDENT MARKET MONITOR FOR PJM

       Pursuant to Rule 211 of the Commission’s Rules and Regulations, 1 Monitoring

Analytics, LLC, acting in its capacity as the Independent Market Monitor (“Market Monitor”)

for PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”), 2 submits these comments responding to the filing

on August 12th, 2026 (“August 12th Filing”), requesting approval of a proposed transaction

under Section 203 of the Federal Power Act in which KKR will acquire EDF’s renewable

energy operations and assets in North America. The August 12th Filing requests approval of

a proposed transaction (“Transaction”) in which KKR Lafayette Buyer, Inc. (“KKR Buyer”),

controlled by KKR & Co. Inc. (“KKR”), will purchase 100 percent of the equity interest in EDF

power solutions, Inc. (“EDFps”) and EDF power solutions Canada Inc. from EDF power

solutions SA (“EDF”). Applicants in the August 12th Filing are EDFps and KKR Buyer

(“Applicants”). KKR has a significant investment in data center development, and the

Transaction creates the risk that capacity will be removed from the PJM market to serve data

center load, contrary to the public interest. 3 The Market Monitor recommends that the

Transaction not be approved unless KKR commits to keep the EDF capacity in the PJM

markets.

       EDF owns 938 MW of generation in PJM. KKR owns 543 MW of generation in PJM

including planned generation. The affiliates of EDF in PJM that are subject to the Transaction

(“EDF Project Companies”) are: EDF Spring Field WPC, LLC (“EDF Spring Field”), Fox

Squirrel Solar LLC (“Fox Squirrel”), Kelly Creek Wind, LLC (“Kelly Creek”), and Pilot Hill

Wind, LLC (“Pilot Hill”). The total generation capacity of the EDF Project Companies is 938

add 700 MW of generation in Texas and Ohio. 5 It is unclear what portion of the 700 MW

       KKR is one of the largest private equity firms in the world and is also a co-owner of

CyrusOne Inc. (“CyrusOne”), a global hyperscale data center developer, together with Global

Infrastructure Partners (“GIP”) which is owned by BlackRock, Inc. (“BlackRock”). 6

According to its website, CyrusOne currently operates multiple data centers in PJM with 398

MW capacity plus two data centers in development. 7 KKR also launched a data center

developer, Helix Digital Infrastructure, with the Kuwait Investment Authority (“KIA”),

NVIDIA Corporation (“NVIDA”) and Vistra Corp. (“Vistra”) in June 2026. 8 In addition, KKR

is a part of the strategic partnerships led by NVIDIA with Apollo Global Management, Inc.,

BlackRock, Inc., Blackstone Inc., Brookfield Corporation, and the Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.

“to mobilize over $500 billion … for the buildout of AI infrastructure over time.” 9

       KKR’s presence in the PJM market is growing as both a data center developer and a

generation owner. The essential point that the filing does not clarify is exactly how KKR will

use its capacity in PJM in the future or use its wide network of direct and indirect ownership

and partnerships in PJM. Applicants do not explain whether KKR intends to use the capacity

to serve data center load directly or whether KKR intends to keep the capacity and energy in

the PJM markets. The lack of such detail in the filing highlights the need for conditions in any

I. COMMENTS

       Removing the capacity from the market would be a form of withholding. Physical

withholding through uneconomic retirement or to directly serve data center load are among

possible mechanisms to exercise market power. The acquisition of generation assets by KKR

in the Transaction creates a clear potential for this form of withholding by removing the

generation from the PJM capacity and energy markets and dedicating the generation to serve

its own data center load. The result would be to make the PJM markets less competitive and

increase costs for other customers. The Market Monitor recommends that the Transaction be

approved only with the condition that the full generation capacity and associated energy of

EDF Project Companies stay in the PJM markets. The Transaction as filed creates the clear

potential that market power will be exercised. As a result, the application has not been shown

to be consistent with the public interest. The Transaction should not be approved without a

commitment from KKR not to remove the EDF Project Companies’ capacity and energy from

the PJM markets to serve data center load.

       KKR is one of the biggest investors in data centers and related infrastructure

developments, in the world and in the PJM region. KKR’s role in data centers creates the

potential that KKR could attempt to remove their generation from the PJM markets in order

to directly serve data center loads. Such arrangements threaten the reliability and economics

of the PJM market by making the PJM markets even shorter and less reliable than they are

now.

       The Market Monitor recognizes that all the EDF Project Companies are under PPAs.

However, the existence of these PPAs does not guarantee that the associated resources will

remain in the PJM Capacity Market. No applicable law or regulation prohibits them from

amending or terminating the PPAs, or from designating the capacity to directly serve data

center load.



                                             -5-
         The impact on competition and reliability of the massive and sudden growth of load

from data centers is the most critical issue affecting PJM markets and the public interest in

competitive outcomes today. A comprehensive solution has not been defined. In the

meantime, consolidation in the markets continues and is evaluated transaction by

transaction. The Commission was in a similar situation in 1996 when it adopted the Merger

Policy Statement. 10 Open access was the overriding issue at that time, and the Commission

exercised its conditioning authority to make open access a condition for approval of

mergers. 11 The Commission’s conditioning authority can and should be invoked today to

address a new issue requiring priority attention. The condition recommended by the Market

Monitor, a commitment to not remove resources from the PJM markets to directly serve data

centers is less burdensome than the requirement to provide open access was in the mid 1990s.

Applicants have provided no information on how the inclusion of such a commitment would

affect their plans, if at all.

        The 2026/2027, 2027/2028 and 2028/2029 Base Residual Auctions (“BRAs”) resulted in

capacity procurement shortfalls, falling below PJM's installed reserve margin in three

minor exceptions, prior to the current extreme conditions in the capacity market. The current

market shortage conditions due to growing data center load have amplified that market

of withholding and result in PJM market prices that exceed the competitive level. The Market

Monitor has documented and quantified the negative impact of data center loads on the

competitiveness of the capacity market and on the prices in the capacity market for PJM

customers in the last three BRAs.15 The Market Monitor has also documented and quantified

 the negative impact of data center loads removing capacity from the capacity market on the

competitiveness of the capacity and energy markets and prices in the capacity and energy

markets. 16 There is, thus, significant evidence in the record showing the adverse impact on

competition in the capacity market and in the energy market that would result from the

removal of resources from the markets to serve data centers. Removal of capacity from the

capacity market would also make PJM less reliable. The fact that PJM is already short of its

reliability target and that PJM faces very significant levels of forecast data center load makes

this reliability impact an even greater risk. Allowing the removal of capacity to serve data

center load would shift the costs and risks of data centers to other PJM customers. This is

inconsistent with the policy goal of ensuring that data centers do not impose their costs and

risks on other customers. 17

       The current rules in the PJM tariff do not explicitly address the removal of capacity

resources from the capacity market to serve data center load. Although the Market Monitor

does not agree, PJM staff have publicly stated that the deactivation rules that define the PJM

analysis and the Market Monitor analysis of proposed deactivations and their conclusions do

 not apply to the removal of resources to serve data center load. 18 For example, if the

deactivation rules do not apply, PJM does not have to make a reliability determination and

the Market Monitor does not have to make a market power determination. For example, if

the deactivation rules do not apply, there are no rules governing Section V (RMR) status for

resources that would exit the market to serve data center load.

       The scope of this proceeding does not include revising or supplementing PJM’s

market rules. The PJM market rules define the context within which the impact of the

Transaction must be evaluated. 19 The existing rules do not address or mitigate the potential

adverse impact on competition from the removal of resources from the markets to serve data

center loads, a reasonably foreseeable consequence of the Transaction. A commitment by the

Applicants to not remove resources from the PJM markets to serve data centers could address

this issue, protect the public interest and would have no impact on the Applicants if they

have no plans to engage in this behavior. Agreement to this condition would be a sign of

good faith by KKR as to its intentions in the PJM markets and broadly consistent with the

Pledge and Principles.

       KKR should be required to agree that KKR will not remove any assets from the PJM

Capacity Market to serve data center load.

       The White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge and the Principles issued by the

National Energy Dominance Council and the PJM Governors make explicit that new data

 Capacity Market would be directly counter to the Pledge and the Principles, would shift risks

        The Market Monitor recommends that the Transaction be approved only with the

 condition that the full generation capacity of EDF Project Companies stays in the PJM

 markets. The Transaction as filed does not provide assurance that market power will not be

 exercised.

 II. CONCLUSION

        The Market Monitor respectfully requests that the Commission afford due

 consideration to this answer as the Commission resolves the issues raised in this proceeding.
